sample_unit: in vivo cases (patients) undergoing flexible ureteroscopy

links.outcome: Patient-level stone type diagnostic accuracy in internal in vivo versus external validation cohorts
links.effect: In vivo (100 cases) and external validation (80 cases) showed diagnostic accuracy of 92.2-95.3% and 86.8-92.2%, respectively, for patient-level stone type prediction, outperforming expert surgeons.
links.quote: In vivo and external validation of 100 and 80 cases, respectively, demonstrated diagnostic accuracy (92.2-95.3% and 86.8-92.2%, respectively) for patient-level stone type prediction, outperforming expert surgeons.

links.outcome: AI stone type prediction accuracy compared with expert surgeons
links.effect: AiFURS patient-level stone type accuracy of 92.2-95.3% (in vivo) and 86.8-92.2% (external) outperformed expert surgeons.
links.quote: In vivo and external validation of 100 and 80 cases, respectively, demonstrated diagnostic accuracy (92.2-95.3% and 86.8-92.2%, respectively) for patient-level stone type prediction, outperforming expert surgeons.

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and clinical validity of a real-time computer vision system during flexible ureteroscopic surgery using ex vivo, in vivo, and external validation datasets, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or implementation practice.
